subject: Private Cluster: node-fleet sizing, IO guardrails, and rollback playbook
messages:
From: Laura Nash <laura.nash@greystone.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: EngOps <engops@greystone.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private cluster intake - node sizing and storage questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the intake call earlier. We're pulling together the internal sprint to onboard Redwood into our private VPC/on-prem footprint. A couple of items came up that we want your team to validate before we commit to hardware: 

- Node sizing for mixed workload (inference + batch transforms) — we expect occasional bursts of long sequences up to 2k tokens.
- Local NVMe vs. network-attached blockstore for KV cache and model artifacts.
- Retention/backup requirements: legal requires 90-day audit logs and 30-day model checkpoints.

Can you share a recommended node fleet mix (GPU counts/types, CPU/memory ratios) and an IO guardrail checklist to confirm we won't hit eviction during inference spikes? Also please include a short rollback/playbook in case a new model rollout causes latency regressions.

We'd appreciate something concrete by Monday so we can finalize procurement.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Nash | Head of Engineering Operations
Greystone Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Laura Nash <laura.nash@greystone.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, EngOps <engops@greystone.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private cluster intake - node sizing and storage questions

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marissa and Karthik from our On‑Prem delivery team for sizing and IO policy notes. We'll produce: a node-fleet recommendation spreadsheet, a short IO guardrail checklist, and a 1-page rollback/playbook.

Quick notes while we scope it:
- Workload profile: small-batch online inference + scheduled heavy transforms implies two node classes:
  * latency nodes (1–2 GPUs, pin to low-latency NICs, high mem)
  * throughput nodes (4–8 GPUs, optimized for batch)
- For KV cache and model artifacts we usually recommend:
  * model artifacts on replicated blockstore (RBD/NFS backed by SAN) with local read cache on NVMe
  * KV cache on ephemeral NVMe on latency nodes (fast local reads + automatic warmup)
- Retention: logs -> long-term object store (S3-compatible) with 90-day retention; checkpoints -> daily snapshot to blockstore + 30-day lifecycle

Marissa / Karthik — can you take ownership of the spreadsheet and guardrails doc? Laura: we can aim to deliver the artifacts by EOD Monday (Nov 16 US business hours). If that works, we'll also schedule a 30-minute sync Tuesday morning to run through runbooks.

Jonas
Jonas Weber | Solutions Architect, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Nov 13, 2026 at 16:05 Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marissa / Karthik — can you take ownership of the spreadsheet and guardrails doc?

Thanks — I'll own the sizing spreadsheet and the IO guardrails checklist. High level follow-ups / assumptions before I start:

1) Burst profile: can you confirm burst frequency (daily peak vs weekly)? That changes how much KV cache we pre-warm.
2) Model mix: primary models are 60% small-parameter (7B family) and 40% medium (30B). Quantization planned?
3) Network: is cross-rack bandwidth limited / egress metered? If egress is expensive, we push more local NVMe caching.

Preliminary recommendations (quick sketch):
- Node classes (example):
  * small-latency: 1x A40-equivalent GPU, 384 GB RAM, 2x 25Gb NIC (for low jitter), 2x 2TB NVMe (for KV + local model cache)
  * medium-throughput: 4x A100/80GB class, 1.5TB RAM aggregate, 10Gb uplink per GPU node, smaller local NVMe (1TB) with primary artifacts on blockstore
- Storage layout:
  * Model artifacts: blockstore (replicated) with SHA256 checksums + versioned S3 copies for recovery
  * KV cache: ephemeral NVMe sized to expected working set (recommend 500–1,000 GB on latency nodes)
  * Backups: nightly snapshots to blockstore + weekly export to S3-compatible object store
- Eviction guardrails:
  * K8s QoS: reserve CPU/memory across pods, priorityClass for inference-critical pods
  * Pod disruption budgets aligned to cluster capacity (don’t allow >20% of latency nodes to drain simultaneously)

I'll turn this into the spreadsheet (redwood-nodegrid-sizing.xlsx) and the checklist (io-guardrails-checklist.md). Karthik, I'll ping you about rollback playbook steps — we want automated traffic-shift and an immediate canary abort path.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | On-Prem Delivery Lead
Redwood Inference
